stem: James has increased work of breathing and hypoxia in the context of reduced left-sided air entry, reduced left chest wall movement, and a hyperresonant percussion note. Which one of the following is this clinically suspicious of?
explanation: Reduced breath sounds, reduced chest movement, hyperresonance, and hypoxia after trauma are classic for a pneumothorax, and in this context it may be tension pneumothorax if the patient is deteriorating.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: Preserved the existing options because one option is clearly the best answer and the stem is already suitable as a single-best-answer item.

optionExplanations.A: Massive haemothorax typically causes dullness to percussion rather than hyperresonance.
optionExplanations.B: Great vessel injury is a major blunt trauma concern but does not classically present with unilateral hyperresonance.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. The combination of unilateral reduced air entry, reduced chest movement, hyperresonance, and hypoxia is most consistent with pneumothorax.
optionExplanations.D: Diaphragmatic rupture may cause bowel sounds in the chest or abnormal abdominal/chest findings, not hyperresonance as the key feature.

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
